entries.description: village must have been founded some time between 1650 and 1700
entries.subject: village must
entries.object: been founded some time between 1650 and 1700

spans.text: The scholarly literature shows that the village must have been founded some time between 1650 and 1700, and that the core of its population consisted of Kikongo speakers (Schwegler 1998, 2006a, 2006b, 2011a).

entries.description: Palenque had always been a place where only few outsiders ventured
entries.subject: Palenque
entries.object: always been a place where only few outsiders ventured

spans.text: Until very recently, Palenque had always been a place where only few outsiders ventured.

entries.task_id: its creole|was|heavily stigmatized and viewed as “backwards”
entries.description: its creole was heavily stigmatized and viewed as “backwards”
entries.subject: its creole

spans.text: Throughout much of the 20th century, its creole was heavily stigmatized and viewed as “backwards”, even by Palenqueros (de Friedemann & Patiño 1983; Schwegler & Morton 2003).

entries.task_id: it|is|important to note
entries.description: It is important to note
entries.subject: It

spans.text: It is important to note, however, that starting around the year 2000, an astonishing reversal of fortunes has taken place, giving Palenquero renewed vigour (Schwegler 2011b).

entries.description: of fortunes has taken place

spans.text: It is important to note, however, that starting around the year 2000, an astonishing reversal of fortunes has taken place, giving Palenquero renewed vigour (Schwegler 2011b).

entries.task_id: when palenquero|was|shunned
entries.description: when Palenquero was shunned
entries.subject: when Palenquero

spans.text: Many adolescents now take great pleasure in learning the creole, and gone are the days when Palenquero (and with it local culture) was shunned.

entries.task_id: papiamentu|is|palenquero’s closest relative
entries.description: Papiamentu is Palenquero’s closest relative
entries.subject: Papiamentu

spans.text: Typologically as well as geographically, Papiamentu is Palenquero’s closest relative, but mutual intelligibility between the two languages would be tenuous at best (Palenque and the islands where Papiamentu is spoken [i.e. Aruba, Bonaire, and Curaçao] have never had any significant social contact).

entries.subject: characterize Atlantic

spans.text: At the same time Palenquero lacks some serial verbs and other features that characterize Atlantic creoles (Holm & Patrick 2007, feature 14).

entries.subject: As

spans.text: As is well known, serialization is common in many West African languages, but rare in the Bantu family (to which Kikongo belongs).

entries.description: these emigrados have tended to shun the creole
entries.subject: these emigrados

spans.text: Despite clustering in socially cohesive barrios, in their new environment these emigrados have tended to shun the creole.

entries.task_id: sociocultural changes|have|significantly facilitated access to palenque
entries.description: sociocultural changes have significantly facilitated access to Palenque
entries.subject: sociocultural changes

spans.text: Improved public transportation and recent sociocultural changes (Schwegler 2011+a) have significantly facilitated access to Palenque, thus strengthening its linguistic and sociocultural ties with the diaspora.

entries.subject: and
entries.object: become an academic tourist mecca of sorts

spans.text: Palenque has gained national as well as international fame, and has become an academic tourist mecca of sorts.

entries.task_id: de sandoval|made|clear in his enlightening de instauranda aethiopum salute
entries.description: de Sandoval made clear in his enlightening De instauranda aethiopum salute
entries.subject: de Sandoval
entries.object: clear in his enlightening De instauranda aethiopum salute

spans.text: As such, Cartagena was the “blackest” and most ethnically diverse city in the New World, a fact that the well-informed contemporary observer Alonso de Sandoval made clear in his enlightening De instauranda aethiopum salute.

entries.task_id: west africa|arrived|in the city
entries.description: West Africa arrived in the city
entries.subject: West Africa

spans.text: During Cartagena’s heyday, bozales (newly imported slaves) from virtually every corner of West and Central West Africa arrived in the city, thereby contributing to an unusually rich situation of New World multilingualism (over seventy African languages were spoken locally).

entries.description: Maroonage was common
entries.subject: Maroonage

spans.text: Maroonage was common, and during the 17th century small groups of escaped slaves managed to establish their first palenques (fortifications) in Cartagena’s hinterland (Navarrete 2003, 2008a, 2008b, n.d.).

entries.subject: Black

spans.text: Contrary to what occurred elsewhere in the Americas, in the Cartagena hinterland, Black maroons rarely joined forces with American Indians (Borrego Plá 1973: 27).

entries.description: the Spanish established the city
entries.subject: the Spanish

spans.text: Moreover, American Indian languages vanished early in the Cartagena area, mainly because indigenous communities were decimated soon after the Spanish established the city.
